title: Chris's first horn and why he never left New Orleans
summary: A woman bought Chris his first horn; he broke it, got another, played with Celestin, and stayed home for his family instead of travelling like Louis.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Well, who was it that gave Chris his first horn? Nutter Rich.

Who was she? Well, at the time she was a lady that was making a little money in the street at the time. Money was easy to get by in those days, you see. Uh-huh. And my daddy had a very short horn, about this horn. And when he bucked his first job, he bucked a guy called Celestan. Celestan was playing on the truck. Uh-huh.
Well, my old man did so good. Uh-huh. I told him, you know, the girls was wild noseda. Uh-huh. She told me, say, see you, buy your home.

See, man with a mirror, buy your home safe. Well, at that period of time, $110 wasn't a lot of money. Oh, yeah. So she bought a good one home for a hundred and ten dollars. And it was really cool. I mean, that period of time, you know, cause there's no money now. But I mean, then it was, you know, plenty more than you. So she gave him a hundred and ten dollars next morning to buy my home. So he bought a good one home with flowers in it. And he blew the bag off. And he blew the bag off. And he blew the bag off. And he blew the bag off. And he blew the bag off. And he blowed the bell off her. He was too powerful for her. Alright, so he had no more horn for about a week's time. So my grandmother, she was a two-headed woman. She said, boss, you can't buy your own horn. She said, I'm going to give you some of the $5. At that time, you can run the pawn shop and get more than that. So we went off the pawn shop and got him another one, you know. But when you look again, that he had a horn that cost $500. Now where that money comes from, I couldn't turn. He was getting robbed, you know what I mean? Yeah, yeah, yeah. He had a real horn, you know. He was rough boy out there. He was in the field. So they got so, right there, wouldn't have to do with him no more. Celestine couldn't do nothing with him no more. Nobody. He was in the field by himself. But I would say he would have always went away and made more of himself than he did. But really, the man was in love with me. I was a child. As far as I know, you know, he was a man that loved it made me. He wouldn't go nowhere, you know. And so he was crazy about my mother and me. So he just wasn't interested. But he made Keller's love behind his own name. He played that all through Orleans Street and everywhere else. He said, a woman, they're called Lula White, heard it and she went away and recorded it. Off of his name, but what you gonna do about it? He just wouldn't go nowhere. Wow. He said, as long as I can make a living here for Papa, which is me, and my mother's name is Ebner, you know. He said, I can make a living for them. I ain't worried about it. He just didn't do anything at that. He wouldn't go nowhere. He wouldn't go nowhere. So he would have been a great man if he would have went away like Lewis did.

Now see, now Lewis and my daddy, all those guys, man, they played around the basin over there. And they had a lot of fun. Loved a lot of homes. And he just had a certain power to him, but Lewis had to ask you to go away, but I mean, he just didn't.
